title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-17
korean_summary: 내일 핵심(화): 관청 조서 법인장 결정 후 이번 주 서명, 15시 산재 치료비 지급 방식 자료·설비 목록 회수(본사 회신 수), 3개월 예상손익 착수(금주 본사). 지난주 시험 답 없음.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Tuesday, November seventeenth. This is your English briefing for today.

Yesterday was a busy Monday. You sent the October results to my director and to the head office, and you closed the firewood report. So today we can focus on a few new things. We have seven parts. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is the closing. One more note. Your Saturday test sheet was empty, so there was no grading this week. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. The record from the authority.

What is it? Yesterday afternoon, the chief accountant answered your three questions. First, the penalty follows a new rule from last December. For this number of invoices, there is a range, and the authority chose the middle of that range. So your earlier range was based on the old rule. Second, two of the invoices are not really ours. One was a sample from our sister company. The other was raw material for a customer. Third, she already explained our situation to the authority, but they would not lower the penalty.

Why is it important? The record must be signed and sent back this week. My director has not approved it yet. Also, even without the two wrong invoices, the rest is still enough. That is the same range, so the penalty would not change. But the record should still be correct.

Your first action today. Report to my director this morning and get his decision. Then ask the chief accountant to ask the authority to remove the two invoices from the record before you sign. The export-import manager still owes you the full check of all documents. That is due on Thursday.
Number two. Medical costs for work accidents.

What is it? The risk management team at the head office wants a change. Right now, an injured worker pays the hospital first, and the company pays them back later. Under the safety law, the company must pay first. The head office wants our plan and our schedule by tomorrow, Wednesday.
Why is it important? This is a legal risk, and every factory got the same request. Our answer should show real numbers, not just a promise.

Your first action today. In the morning, check with the HR manager that she and the factory nurse have started. Their answer is due at three o'clock. They need three things. The accident cases from the last twelve months. Whether one or two hospitals can bill the company monthly. And if not, whether we can leave a deposit at the hospital. After three o'clock, write the draft reply to the head office.
Number three. The forecast for November to January.

What is it? Yesterday my director confirmed the October results. He also wrote that the forecast for the next three months must go to the head office this week. You already told the planning team that you will send it this week.
Why is it important? The week is short. If you start on Thursday, there is no time for my director to review it.
Your first action today. Open the forecast file and update it with the October actual numbers. Try to show a first draft to my director by Thursday.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the maintenance staff. The head office asked us to add common equipment to the machine list. That means the compressor, the air tank, the boiler, and so on. You asked her to check your file and answer by three o'clock today. You can say this. Could you let me know where the machine list stands? I need it by three o'clock.

Second, the HR manager and the new sewer test. From today, every new sewer takes a grade test within three days after joining. The production director approved it yesterday. Check that the form reached the line leaders and the trainers. You can say this. Please send me the results of the first group by Thursday.

Third, the HR staff. Yesterday you sent her more items from the attendance check. One worker has stopped coming to work. But she is still active in the system. You can say this. Did she resign? If yes, please update her status today.

Fourth, the IT staff. Yesterday you told him to go ahead with round one of the camera hard disks. He needs a quote first, and then a purchase request. You can say this. Please send me the quote and the purchase request for round one this week.

Fifth, the fabric warehouse manager. Yesterday you asked her to try the new system instead of the hand record. She should split the fabric line by yards for each style. Only the yards must be correct. Check whether she tried it with the next fabric lot. You can say this. Did you split the next lot in the system? Please send me a screenshot.
Sixth, the cost accountant. You sent her the confirmed October profit and loss. Now she makes the profit and loss for each buyer. Just check that she has started.
Seventh, the weekly consumables report. The maintenance staff writes it every Tuesday now. Read it, and ask only two or three questions.
Eighth, a fusing machine belt. You asked a Korean manager at another company for a quote. If he answers, compare it with the two quotes you already have.
Part three. Replies you owe.
First, my director, about the official record. Your message can start like this. I would like to bring the official record to your attention. We need to sign it this week.
Second, a head office manager. The reply on medical costs is due tomorrow. Your reply can start like this. Thank you for your guidance. Here is our current process and our plan to change it.

Third, Another head office manager. He needs the updated machine list by tomorrow. After the maintenance staff answers, send it. Your reply can start like this. Please find the updated machine list with the common equipment added.

Fourth, the mending companies. A head office manager sent guidance on Saturday. Read it carefully. If you agree, a short reply is enough. You can start like this. Thank you for the guidance. We will follow it from this month.
Fifth, a production manager. On Saturday he asked three more questions about the dummies. Your reply can start like this. To clarify, I'm asking about the covers only, not the whole dummy.
Sixth, the compliance officer. She sent the comparison quote for the electrical inspection on Saturday. Review it, and tell her whether the scope is the same in each quote.
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Tuesday. The new sewer test starts. The HR manager and the maintenance staff answer at three o'clock. The short-term workers' pay goes out. Check the CAD room daily report at nine o'clock. The financial statement update for the head office is also due around today.
Wednesday, November eighteenth. The reply on medical costs and the machine list go to the head office. The weekly headcount update. And the warehouse's interlining upload.

Thursday, November nineteenth. The full declaration check from the export-import manager. The compliance officer's new quote for fire system maintenance. The overtime report for next week. And the curtain materials for the storage area arrive.
One more date. The labor agreement ends next Tuesday, November twenty-fourth. Ask the HR manager where the registration stands.
Part five. English review.
We will review eight expressions from your recent cards. Listen, and then say each one out loud.

Number one. The expression is, defer. It means to move a decision or a purchase to later. For example, we will defer the replacement until the drive fails. Now say it with me. We will defer the replacement until the drive fails.
One more time. We will defer the replacement until the drive fails.

Number two. The expression is, in three phases. A phase is one step of a bigger job. For example, we will replace the hard disks in three phases. Now say it with me. We will replace the hard disks in three phases.
One more time. We will replace the hard disks in three phases.

Number three. The expression is, acknowledge. It means to accept that something is true. For example, we acknowledge the late invoices, but two of them are not ours. Now say it with me. We acknowledge the late invoices, but two of them are not ours.
One more time. We acknowledge the late invoices, but two of them are not ours.

Number four. The expression is, given that something, we will do something. It means because of this fact. For example, given that the penalty is the same, we will sign the record this week. Now say it with me. Given that the penalty is the same, we will sign the record this week.
One more time. Given that the penalty is the same, we will sign the record this week.

Number five. The expression is, I would like to bring something to your attention. It is a polite way to report a problem. For example, I would like to bring the official record to your attention. Now say it with me. I would like to bring the official record to your attention.
One more time. I would like to bring the official record to your attention.

Number six. The expression is, comparable. It means you can compare two things because the conditions are the same. For example, please get comparable quotes for the same scope. Now say it with me. Please get comparable quotes for the same scope.
One more time. Please get comparable quotes for the same scope.

Number seven. The expression is, oversee. It means to be responsible and watch over something. For example, the nurse will oversee the medical cost records. Now say it with me. The nurse will oversee the medical cost records.
One more time. The nurse will oversee the medical cost records.

Number eight. The expression is, to clarify, I'm asking about this, not just that. You use it when someone misunderstood your question. For example, to clarify, I'm asking about the last twelve months, not just this month. Now say it with me. To clarify, I'm asking about the last twelve months, not just this month.
One more time. To clarify, I'm asking about the last twelve months, not just this month.
Good. Try to use one of these in a real email today. The best one is number five, in your message to my director.
Part six. Role-play.
This morning you will talk to my director about the official record. Listen to the conversation first.
Anthony says. Good morning. I would like to bring the official record to your attention. We need to sign it this week.
My director says. Okay. Did the chief accountant find out how they calculated the penalty?
Anthony says. Yes. A new rule started this year. For this number of invoices, there is a range. The authority chose the middle.
My director says. Can we ask for a lower amount?
Anthony says. The chief accountant already asked. They did not agree. But there is one more point. Two of the invoices are not ours.
My director says. Whose are they?
Anthony says. One was a sample from our sister company. The other was material for a customer. We were not aware of these documents until the authority found them.
My director says. Does it change the penalty?
Anthony says. No. The rest is still in the same range. But I want the record to be correct before we sign.
My director says. Good. Then ask them to remove the two, and sign it this week.
Anthony says. Yes. Given that the amount is the same, I will not argue more about the penalty. I will also ask the sales team to tell us before they send any sample.
My director says. Okay. Let me know when it is signed.
That is the end of the conversation. Now repeat two key sentences.
Sentence one. We were not aware of these documents until the authority found them.
One more time. We were not aware of these documents until the authority found them.
Sentence two. Given that the amount is the same, I will not argue more about the penalty.
One more time. Given that the amount is the same, I will not argue more about the penalty.
Now three short sentences you can use with your team today. Say each one after me.
For the HR manager. Please send me the hospital answers by three o'clock.
For the maintenance staff. Could you let me know where the machine list stands?
For the IT staff. Please send me the quote and the purchase request for round one.
And two sentences for the head office. Listen first.
For the head office. Here is our current process and our plan to change it. We will start the new way once the hospital agrees.
One more time. Here is our current process and our plan to change it.
For the planning team. The forecast for November to January will be ready by Friday. I will send it after my director reviews it.
One more time. I will send it after my director reviews it.
Well done.
Part seven. Closing.

Let me say the most important thing one more time. Get my director's decision on the official record this morning, collect the hospital and machine answers at three o'clock, and start the three-month forecast.
Three things, in that order. The rest can wait.
Have a good Tuesday, Anthony. See you tomorrow.
